evals.prompt: Let's do a deep dive into CVA. I don't know anything about it. Create me a guided tour on how CVA is used in the app, given I don't know how it's used in the app. You should explain me what it is, how it works, and how it's implemented in the app. Ask me relevant questions to test my knowledge after each section of the guided tour
evals.expected_output: A brief concept intro (3 paragraphs max) explaining what CVA is and why it exists. Then Section 1 only — a real code snippet from the codebase, an explanation, and a concrete quiz question. The response must stop there and wait for the user's answer.

assertions.text: The response references at least one real file from the codebase (e.g. badge.tsx, button.tsx) by name — not just generic library docs
A real code snippet from the codebase is shown inline (not just a file path reference)
There is a brief plain-language intro explaining what CVA is and why it exists before the code tour begins
The response contains only Section 1 — it does NOT dump all sections at once (file must be under ~80 lines)
The response ends with a concrete, specific quiz question about the code just shown
The quiz question references a specific element from the code snippet shown (a variant name, a function call, a prop, etc.)
